claims.text: The reported HfNbTiVAl10 state has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase-separated domains.
A physics-informed neural-network model using multiscale microstructural descriptors and reduced-order simulations can predict Young's modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model can predict the yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model can predict the toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Spatial phase distributions, local chemical inhomogeneities, and estimated slip-system orientations will be used as model inputs.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates localized stress distributions.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates dislocation dynamics.
The selected microstructural descriptors capture the stress distributions and dislocation dynamics relevant to macroscopic mechanical response.
Physics-based constraints and microstructure-informed features allow reduced-order simulations to extrapolate effective mechanical properties without exhaustive computations.
Local elastic moduli govern the predicted Young's modulus.
Obstacle strengths to dislocation motion govern the predicted yield strength.
Crack-initiation sites govern the predicted fracture toughness.
The proposed model will reduce RMSE by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional approaches for Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by approximately one order of magnitude relative to prior methods.
Full CALPHAD and first-principles methods impose high computational demands.
Existing methods have limited predictive accuracy for fracture-related properties.
The model may become unreliable when measured descriptors are not representative of the actual hierarchical heterogeneity.
The model may become unreliable when previously unseen phases or defects dominate mechanical response.
The model may become unreliable outside its calibrated temperature and strain-rate regimes.
A blinded benchmark will falsify the hypothesis if any targeted property fails to obtain the specified 20–30% RMSE improvement or if the speedup is less than tenfold.
